After years of inflating boards by hand, I finally made the switch to an electric pump — and honestly, I should have done it much sooner. If you ask me, it’s the best accessory upgrade you can make to your paddleboard setup. What used to take 15 minutes of hard work now happens while I sort my kit and check the conditions. My arms are saved for actually paddling.
Most inflatable paddle boards come with a manual pump as standard, and they do the job — but they’re exhausting, especially if you’re inflating more than one board or heading out regularly. Electric SUP pumps solve this completely. You set your target PSI, press a button, and walk away. Modern pumps get a standard board to 15 PSI in 8–12 minutes; the faster battery-powered models can do it in under five.
This best electric pump for paddle boards guide covers six pumps across the full range — from a straightforward budget option under £50 to the quickest battery-powered pump currently available. I’ve tested several of these personally, and I’m clear about which ones I haven’t when it comes to the assessments. Use the comparison table to narrow things down, then read the full entry for the ones that interest you.

I’ve had the Shark 3 on my radar for a while. On paper — and from what early testing shows — this is a significant step up from the Shark II it replaces. The speed is the headline: where most 12V pumps take 8–12 minutes, the Shark 3 does it in under five on battery. For busy mornings or back-to-back sessions with the family, that difference adds up fast.
The dual-power setup is a smart piece of design. If you forget to charge it before leaving the house, plug it into the car’s 12V socket and it still works — just at the slower pace of a standard electric pump rather than stopping entirely. The battery also charges fully in two hours with a 45W fast charger.
The trade-off is the weight. At around 2.9kg, it’s noticeably heavier than most 12V pumps on this list, and the housing is larger to accommodate the battery and cooling mechanisms. For most paddlers, this won’t matter — it goes in the boot and stays there — but if you’re packing light for travel it’s worth considering.
The three preset inflation modes with memory recall mean you can save settings for each piece of kit. Once you’ve set it up the first time, the routine is quick.

The Wave Electric Pump (A.K.A Airbank Puffer Pro) is a battery-powered, dual-stage pump small enough to go wherever your paddle board goes. At about the size of a kid’s lunchbox, it fits in a small drybag, so I can carry a deflated board to spots too far from the car park for a mains or 12V-only pump, then paddle off with the pump on the deck.
It took 11 minutes to inflate my Wave Cruiser to 15 PSI. That’s a little over Wave’s claimed 8–10 minutes, but in line with most electric pumps. On a single charge, it inflates four boards to 15 PSI, and the auto shut-off cut off the instant it hit the PSI I’d set. There’s a built-in light for late-night paddles, a deflate mode, and it doubles as a power bank for your phone. If the battery does run out, the 12V car plug has you covered.
The trade-off is that there’s no active cooling. After a 20 PSI run, it was noticeably warm, so I’d give it 10–15 minutes to cool down between boards. If you regularly inflate for a group and want it done fast, a bigger pump with active cooling is the better bet. But if you want a cordless pump that goes wherever you paddle, the Wave pump is hard to beat for the size.

An electric pump is one of the best accessories you can purchase for your stand up paddle board. Whether it is your first time on a SUP or you are a professional paddle boarder, you can’t beat the hands-free ease of an electric paddle board pump. We put the most popular electric pumps for paddle boards through thousands of uses to find out which are the Best iSUP Pumps of 2024.
Electric paddle board pumps save you the energy of hand-pumping and help you get on the water faster. Instead of inflating your paddle board by hand and then getting ready to hit the water, you can change clothes, apply sunscreen, fill water bottles, and more all while an electric pump inflates your iSUP.
Electric SUP Pumps are designed specifically for the challenges of inflating a paddle board. They have two stages: a high-flow/low-pressure stage to inflate the board from flat to about 1 PSI and then a low-flow/high-pressure stage that brings your paddle board to its final pressure. Each pump has an automatic cutoff that you can set to your desired pressure. Once the board reaches that pressure, the pump will automatically turn off to prevent over-pressurizing your board.
In the past, electric SUP pumps have required you to connect directly to your car’s battery or plug into a 12v socket (“cigarette lighter”) in your car. But now, many electric pumps with built-in lithium-ion batteries can inflate multiple paddle boards extremely quickly.
Choosing the best electric pump for your paddle board boils down to whether you are looking for speed, portability, ease of use, or a bit of all three. We tested several electric SUP pumps for speed, usability, portability, and other measures. Here is our list of the Best iSUP Pumps.

Outdoor Master Shark III Electric SUP Pump
Availability: US, Canada, Australia, UK, Europe

The Shark III Electric SUP Pump is Outdoor Master’s new Flagship offering. It boasts incredibly fast inflation times and the portability of a built-in battery.
Save
Features and Usability:
The Shark III comes with all the bells and whistles you could hope for. The pump itself has, of course, automatic inflation and deflation capabilities and can bring your board up to 20 PSI. It has an onboard active cooling system and a large LCD Display screen. However, like the Cachalot 2S, the screen is difficult to read in bright daylight.
You can control the pump’s settings with the four buttons located on the top of the pump. The screen indicates battery life remaining with color indicators around the edge of the screen. The Shark III also has different settings for inflating SUPs, Kites/Wings, and Air Mattresses, as well as a memory function to recall your preferred settings.
The biggest downside of the Shark III is its size. At 6.5 pounds and with a voluminous shape, it’s hard to forget where you put the pump.
Inflation Speed:
The Shark III takes over the top spot for the fastest electric pump we’ve reviewed, inflating our test board to 15 PSI in an average of 5 minutes.
Battery and Other Accessories:
The internal 74Wh battery has enough juice to reliably inflate three paddle boards. When the battery gets low, you can plug the Shark III into a 12v power source to operate the pump, though it inflates at a much slower speed than with the battery. The USB-C port can also charge your phone and other devices.
Bottom Line: The Outdoor Master Shark 3 is an ultra-fast and versatile rechargeable electric pump.

Features and Usability:
The Seawolf’s key feature is its massive internal battery. With a 10,000mAh battery, it has more power onboard than some eBikes! The Seawolf’s battery has enough juice to inflate our 11’x32″ test board to 15 PSI seven times and still has a little power left over to deflate them at the end of the day.
The interface is clean and easy to use, with four buttons and an easy-to-read, information-packed screen. There is a power switch on the bottom of the pump to turn the Seawolf on and start the internal cooling fan.
The Seawolf is easy to operate. There is one button to change units from PSI to Bar, +/- buttons to adjust the target pressure (up to 20 PSI), and a power button to start and stop the pump.

After years of inflating boards by hand, I finally made the switch to an electric pump — and honestly, I should have done it much sooner. If you ask me, it’s the best accessory upgrade you can make to your paddleboard setup. What used to take 15 minutes of hard work now happens while I sort my kit and check the conditions. My arms are saved for actually paddling.
Most inflatable paddle boards come with a manual pump as standard, and they do the job — but they’re exhausting, especially if you’re inflating more than one board or heading out regularly. Electric SUP pumps solve this completely. You set your target PSI, press a button, and walk away. Modern pumps get a standard board to 15 PSI in 8–12 minutes; the faster battery-powered models can do it in under five.
This best electric pump for paddle boards guide covers six pumps across the full range — from a straightforward budget option under £50 to the quickest battery-powered pump currently available. I’ve tested several of these personally, and I’m clear about which ones I haven’t when it comes to the assessments. Use the comparison table to narrow things down, then read the full entry for the ones that interest you.

I’ve had the Shark 3 on my radar for a while. On paper — and from what early testing shows — this is a significant step up from the Shark II it replaces. The speed is the headline: where most 12V pumps take 8–12 minutes, the Shark 3 does it in under five on battery. For busy mornings or back-to-back sessions with the family, that difference adds up fast.
The dual-power setup is a smart piece of design. If you forget to charge it before leaving the house, plug it into the car’s 12V socket and it still works — just at the slower pace of a standard electric pump rather than stopping entirely. The battery also charges fully in two hours with a 45W fast charger.
The trade-off is the weight. At around 2.9kg, it’s noticeably heavier than most 12V pumps on this list, and the housing is larger to accommodate the battery and cooling mechanisms. For most paddlers, this won’t matter — it goes in the boot and stays there — but if you’re packing light for travel it’s worth considering.
The three preset inflation modes with memory recall mean you can save settings for each piece of kit. Once you’ve set it up the first time, the routine is quick.

The Wave Electric Pump (A.K.A Airbank Puffer Pro) is a battery-powered, dual-stage pump small enough to go wherever your paddle board goes. At about the size of a kid’s lunchbox, it fits in a small drybag, so I can carry a deflated board to spots too far from the car park for a mains or 12V-only pump, then paddle off with the pump on the deck.
It took 11 minutes to inflate my Wave Cruiser to 15 PSI. That’s a little over Wave’s claimed 8–10 minutes, but in line with most electric pumps. On a single charge, it inflates four boards to 15 PSI, and the auto shut-off cut off the instant it hit the PSI I’d set. There’s a built-in light for late-night paddles, a deflate mode, and it doubles as a power bank for your phone. If the battery does run out, the 12V car plug has you covered.
The trade-off is that there’s no active cooling. After a 20 PSI run, it was noticeably warm, so I’d give it 10–15 minutes to cool down between boards. If you regularly inflate for a group and want it done fast, a bigger pump with active cooling is the better bet. An electric pump is one of the best accessories you can purchase for your stand up paddle board. Whether it is your first time on a SUP or you are a professional paddle boarder, you can’t beat the hands-free ease of an electric paddle board pump. We put the most popular electric pumps for paddle boards through thousands of uses to find out which are the Best iSUP Pumps of 2024.
Electric paddle board pumps save you the energy of hand-pumping and help you get on the water faster. Instead of inflating your paddle board by hand and then getting ready to hit the water, you can change clothes, apply sunscreen, fill water bottles, and more all while an electric pump inflates your iSUP.
Electric SUP Pumps are designed specifically for the challenges of inflating a paddle board. They have two stages: a high-flow/low-pressure stage to inflate the board from flat to about 1 PSI and then a low-flow/high-pressure stage that brings your paddle board to its final pressure. Each pump has an automatic cutoff that you can set to your desired pressure. Once the board reaches that pressure, the pump will automatically turn off to prevent over-pressurizing your board.
In the past, electric SUP pumps have required you to connect directly to your car’s battery or plug into a 12v socket (“cigarette lighter”) in your car. But now, many electric pumps with built-in lithium-ion batteries can inflate multiple paddle boards extremely quickly.
Choosing the best electric pump for your paddle board boils down to whether you are looking for speed, portability, ease of use, or a bit of all three. We tested several electric SUP pumps for speed, usability, portability, and other measures. Here is our list of the Best iSUP Pumps.

The Shark III Electric SUP Pump is Outdoor Master’s new Flagship offering. It boasts incredibly fast inflation times and the portability of a built-in battery.
Save
Features and Usability:
The Shark III comes with all the bells and whistles you could hope for. The pump itself has, of course, automatic inflation and deflation capabilities and can bring your board up to 20 PSI. It has an onboard active cooling system and a large LCD Display screen. However, like the Cachalot 2S, the screen is difficult to read in bright daylight.
You can control the pump’s settings with the four buttons located on the top of the pump. The screen indicates battery life remaining with color indicators around the edge of the screen. The Shark III also has different settings for inflating SUPs, Kites/Wings, and Air Mattresses, as well as a memory function to recall your preferred settings.
The biggest downside of the Shark III is its size. At 6.5 pounds and with a voluminous shape, it’s hard to forget where you put the pump.
Inflation Speed:
The Shark III takes over the top spot for the fastest electric pump we’ve reviewed, inflating our test board to 15 PSI in an average of 5 minutes.
Battery and Other Accessories:
The internal 74Wh battery has enough juice to reliably inflate three paddle boards. When the battery gets low, you can plug the Shark III into a 12v power source to operate the pump, though it inflates at a much slower speed than with the battery. The USB-C port can also charge your phone and other devices.
Bottom Line: The Outdoor Master Shark 3 is an ultra-fast and versatile rechargeable electric pump.

The Seawolf’s key feature is its massive internal battery. With a 10,000mAh battery, it has more power onboard than some eBikes! The Seawolf’s battery has enough juice to inflate our 11’x32″ test board to 15 PSI seven times and still has a little power left over to deflate them at the end of the day.
The interface is clean and easy to use, with four buttons and an easy-to-read, information-packed screen. There is a power switch on the bottom of the pump to turn the Seawolf on and start the internal cooling fan.
The Seawolf is easy to operate. There is one button to change units from PSI to Bar, +/- buttons to adjust the target pressure (up to 20 PSI), and a power button to start and stop the pump.
